headline: Attackers handed hands-on-keyboard intrusion work to an unattended AI agent inside Thailand's finance ministry as a browser-built malvertising wave and an unpatched Fastjson flaw drew live exploitation.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are delegating offensive work to autonomous agents, running the open-source Hermes assistant unattended against Thailand's Ministry of Finance while OpenAI's own models roamed the open internet for days.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hackers Automate a Ministry Breach With an Unattended AI Agent

emerging_trends.text: Malvertising crews increasingly assemble payloads on the victim's own machine, with SourTrade making browsers build Windows executables from pieces to slip past scanners that expect one malicious file.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SourTrade Malvertising Builds Malware Inside the Browser

emerging_trends.text: Server-side code keeps handing attackers unauthenticated remote execution, from the Fastjson library inside Spring Boot apps to crafted SVGs on Bing's image workers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Fastjson RCE Draws Live Attacks Before a Patch

topics.title: SourTrade Malvertising Builds Malware Inside the Browser
topics.latest_developments: Confiant detailed SourTrade on July 23, 2026, a malvertising operation running since late 2024 that impersonates TradingView, Solana, and Luno and makes victims' browsers assemble the final Windows executable from pieces using the legitimate Bun runtime, defeating scanners that expect one complete malicious file at a fixed URL.
topics.summary: SourTrade targets retail cryptocurrency traders through fake ad-driven pages whose JavaScript builds malware directly in browser memory. Block the impersonated domains and flag unexpected Bun runtime execution on endpoints.

sources.title: Malvertising Sends Malware in Pieces, Then Makes the Browser Build the Executable
Malicious sites use JavaScript to build malware in browser memory

topics.title: Malware-as-a-Service Ecosystems Regroup
topics.latest_developments: PRODAFT exposed a centralized DevMan ransomware-as-a-service portal it tracks as Funky Mantis, where affiliates build payloads, manage victims, and track payouts, while the Golden Chickens malware-as-a-service crew resurfaced with four new families: TinyEgg, ChonkyChicken, a modular ChonkyChicken variant, and a reworked browser-credential stealer.
topics.summary: Both operations sell turnkey attack infrastructure to affiliates, lowering the bar for ransomware and credential theft. Monitor for the named families and treat commodity service portals as active threats.

sources.title: DevMan RaaS Portal Centralizes Payload Builds, Victim Management, and Affiliate Payouts
Golden Chickens Resurfaces With Four New Malware Families and Modular Implants

topics.title: Fastjson RCE Draws Live Attacks Before a Patch
topics.latest_developments: ThreatBook and Imperva report attackers exploiting CVE-2026-16723, a 9.0-rated flaw in Alibaba's Fastjson Java library, where a single malicious JSON request runs code without authentication at the privileges of the Java process, and no fix is yet available.
topics.summary: Fastjson parses JSON inside countless Spring Boot applications, exposing affected servers to unauthenticated remote code execution. Filter untrusted JSON, apply Alibaba's mitigations, and move off the 1.x branch.

sources.title: Fastjson 1.x RCE Vulnerability Targeted in Attacks With No Patched Available

topics.title: Hackers Automate a Ministry Breach With an Unattended AI Agent
topics.latest_developments: A threat actor installed the open-source Hermes AI agent on a rented server, switched off its permission prompts, and ran it in unattended "YOLO" mode to automate post-exploitation across Thailand's Ministry of Finance, checking hosts for root, hunting through file systems, and working the treasury-and-tax network on its own.
topics.summary: The Ministry of Finance runs Thailand's treasury and tax collection, and the case marks attackers handing live intrusion work to a commodity AI agent. Restrict outbound access from AI tooling and treat agent activity as privileged.

sources.title: Hermes AI agent used to automate attack on Thai Finance Ministry
Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

topics.title: Crafted SVGs Run as SYSTEM on Bing's Image Servers
topics.latest_developments: XBOW showed that a crafted SVG submitted to Bing's image search ran commands as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Microsoft's production image-processing workers and as root on the Linux machines in the same fleet, prompting Microsoft to issue two critical CVEs, including CVE-2026-32194.
topics.summary: The flaws sat in Bing's image-processing tier, letting attacker-controlled SVG files execute at the highest privilege across Microsoft's server fleet. Microsoft has patched its infrastructure, so customers need take no action.

sources.title: Bing Images Flaws Let Crafted SVGs Run Commands as SYSTEM on Microsoft's Servers

topics.title: BlueNoroff Phishing Kit Profiles Crypto Wallets
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found the North Korean group BlueNoroff running an active phishing kit that impersonates Zoom and Microsoft Teams through typosquatted domains and profiles a target's cryptocurrency wallets before it delivers malware.
topics.summary: BlueNoroff blends compromised industry contacts with ClickFix-style social engineering to steal from crypto holders. Verify meeting links out of band and block typosquatted videoconferencing domains.

sources.title: BlueNoroff Zoom Phishing Kit Profiles Crypto Wallets Before Malware Delivery
